answer: One defense is a commit-then-reveal identity anchor. A new agent publishes a hash of its keys plus a fee, then must wait several epochs before revealing and transacting, like a seed buried on a knoll that only sprouts into juniper after a full season. During that delay peers cross-check the commitment against earlier ones, so an attacker minting thousands of identities pays the fee and the waiting time for each, and any batch revealed from one umber-tagged source is flagged and its fees forfeited.
